newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada grain stocks as of July 31.
newsitem.headline: Canada grain stocks as of July 31.

text.p: Statistics Canada survey of farm and commercial grain stocks on July 31 in millions of tonnes, with farm stocks of a year earlier:
'96 FARM STOCKS '95 FARM STOCKS COMMERCIAL TOTAL

Statistics Canada said stocks of wheat and barley on July 31 were well below the past five-year average, with barley stocks at their lowest level since 1985. Farm stocks of canola were at their highest since 1989 and the third highest on record.

The main reasons for the slight increase of wheat stocks were a six percent reduction in producers' marketing and less wheat fed to livestock, the agency said. Higher demand for feed barley and increased producers' marketing were the main factors behind the low barley stocks.
Increased foreign competition in Canola markets led to higher stocks in Canadian farms, Statistics Canada said.

Canola exports to Europe declined by more than one million tonnes since the same period of 1995, due in part to record canola stocks in Europe. Also, Japan was now buying more canola from Australia, the agency said.
